apparatus.basis: Standard chapter heading restored from bracketed editor's reading
ⲛ̄ⲕⲣ[ⲓ] surviving + ⲧⲏⲥ at start of next line; Greek κριτής 'judge' fits ⲟⲩⲛⲁⲃ ⲛ̄ⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ 'a great judge'
ⲧⲉⲥⲕⲉ visible at line start; sense uncertain — possibly action-noun related to ⲧⲁϩⲟ 'set, place,' or related to ⲥⲕⲉⲡⲥⲓⲥ. Tentative
Editor restoration; standard Manichaean title 'Father of the Greatness' fits the cosmological context

notes.decision: Page number ⲟ̄ = 70. The ⟦ ⟧ marks scribal/transcriptional convention; treated as the page number proper.

Lines 8 and 10 contain scribal cancellations of ⲕⲁ (= 21). The scribe was apparently writing the chapter number 21 for the new kephalaion that begins at line 12, with multiple corrections in the heading area. Treated as lacuna since the canceled text does not represent the intended reading.
Lyc. directional 'upon us' (= Sah. ⲁϫⲱⲛ); fits with κίνδυνοι 'dangers upon us' as standard hardship-formula.
'There being no measure to her' — this stock formula introduces the 'innumerability' theme that runs through the cosmic enumeration of lines 18-23 (sea, firmaments, winds, rivers, dispersed limbs).
Translated 'the two Callings.' Distinct from the Call/Hearing pair — two summonings/emanations are distinguished here. The verb ⲉⲧⲁϩⲧⲁⲍⲙⲟⲩ confirms the act of summoning forth.

Three measure-terms: ⲉϩⲁⲧ 'silver' (used metonymically as 'weight/balance'), ϣⲓ 'measure,' Greek μέτρον 'metron.' Reads as triplet of measuring-instruments — pointing to what cannot be measured even by these.

ⲕⲗⲏⲗ rendered 'wreaths' from the Coptic root ⲕⲗⲟⲙ 'wreath/garland,' here probably 'produce, growth' of the earth in pairing with 'clusters of vines.' Confirmed by line 26 collocation ⲃⲝⲃⲓⲗⲉ ⲛ̄ϣⲱ 'grains of sand' as parallel small-thing register.
'Clusters of the vines' — ⲝⲗⲟⲗⲉ = ϫⲗⲟⲗⲉ 'grape-cluster'; ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲉⲩⲉ = Lyc. plural of ⲉⲗⲟⲟⲗⲉ 'vine.'

'The three rivers'; ⲙⲁⲝⲓⲟⲣⲉ likely Lyc. orthographic variant for 'rivers' (with ⲓⲟⲣ 'river' as core) — possibly 'places of rivers' or compound river-noun. Standard Manichaean cosmology has three or four cosmic rivers surrounding the world.

ⲙⲉⲥⲗⲏⲥ rendered 'limbs' (μέλη with anomalous Lyc. orthography). ⲉⲧϣⲙⲁⲁⲧ provisionally 'dispersed/scattered'; alternative 'honored' from ⲧⲁⲉⲓⲏⲩ is also possible. The dispersed light-limbs are a standard Manichaean cosmological motif.
'Grains/kernels' — paired with ⲛϣⲱ 'sand' in line 26 as small-particle measure. Distinct from ⲡⲃⲣⲉ 'seed.' Likely related to ⲃⲣⲃⲣ 'pebble' or a granular-dimensional term.
'They shall not be likened to him' — ϣⲧⲏⲧⲉ from ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ 'liken, compare,' Lyc. infinitive form with ϣ- circumstantial. ⲁϩⲣ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ = 'as before / as previously.'
ⲥⲉⲍⲉ 'set/raise' + ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲥ̄ 'on her feet' — the standard idiom 'cause her to stand up' (cf. ⲥⲉⲍⲱ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ in accumulated vocabulary). Used here of the Mother(?) being established within his storehouses.
'Stillness and silence' — the ⲍⲣⲁⲕ/ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓⲧϩ pair appears elsewhere as the calm-state of pre-emanation. The Mother dwells in the storehouses in this state until summoned.
'She gazed upon' — ⲃⲱϣⲧ 'look, gaze' + ⲥⲁ 'after, upon.' The Mother surveying her own aeons of light upon emanation.
